Target unit references labor arbitration council regulations. Initial assumption suggests extracting the specific clause governing the number of labor arbitrators. Reviewing the text structure to isolate the exact prescriptive rule from the administrative heading.

Parsing the structural breakdown reveals a governing clause introducing three distinct nominating bodies, totaling at least fifteen labor arbitrators. Each sub-provision dictates a minimum quota of five members designated by provincial labor authorities, provincial trade unions, and local employer representatives respectively.

Analyzing sub-provision components identifies the action as nomination targeting a minimum member quota. Entity classification for provincial trade unions remains ambiguous regarding whether to map them under labor representatives or assign an undefined tag.

Target predicate extraction requires isolating the nominal object determining the member quota from the agentive prepositional phrase. The term "đề cử" functions as the primary verb, while "tối thiểu 05 thành viên" forms the core nominal object, excluding the intervening agentive marker and nominating body subject.

Evaluating span ordering constraints shows that constituent segments must follow sequential text appearance rules rather than inverted grammatical positioning. Re-verifying the core predicate and object extraction confirms that the quantitative requirement functions as the primary nominal object matching the identified verb.

Assigning the agent entity code initially points toward the worker category, but trade unions function as institutional representatives rather than individual workers. Re-evaluating the classification criteria confirms that unmapped entities default to the undefined category. Prepositional markers indicating agency are systematically excluded from the core nominal structure, preserving only the quantitative requirement within the primary predicate span.
